subject: Environment
description: Lantana, Parthenium, water hyacinth, African catfish — pathways, impacts, control

questions.stem: An 'invasive alien species' (IAS) is best defined as:

options.option_text: Any plant or animal not native to a region
A non-native species whose introduction causes economic or ecological harm
A native species that becomes dominant
Any genetically-modified organism

questions.explanation: IUCN definition: an alien species whose introduction and spread threatens biological diversity, food security, plant/animal health or has economic and environmental impact. Key tests — (1) NON-native to the region, (2) ESTABLISHES self-sustaining populations, (3) causes HARM. Many alien species are harmless or beneficial (most crops). Only the harmful ones are 'invasive'. CBD's Aichi Target 9 and KMGBF Target 6 (2022) call on parties to identify, prioritise and control IAS pathways.

questions.stem: 'Lantana camara' — perhaps India's most damaging invasive plant — was introduced to India primarily as:

options.option_text: A medicinal herb
An ornamental garden plant in colonial era
A fodder crop for livestock
A timber tree

questions.explanation: Lantana camara (native to South & Central America) was introduced into Calcutta Botanic Garden by the British in 1809 as an ornamental shrub for its colourful flowers. It escaped cultivation and now infests >40% of India's tiger reserves — outcompetes native vegetation, alters fire regimes, reduces forage for herbivores. Estimated economic damage: ₹900 crore/year. Hard to remove because it resprouts from root crowns; experiments include controlled burning + replanting natives.

questions.stem: 'Congress Grass' — a major weed associated with allergic dermatitis and hay fever in humans — is the common name for:

options.option_text: Eichhornia crassipes
Parthenium hysterophorus
Mikania micrantha
Prosopis juliflora

questions.explanation: Parthenium hysterophorus — also called 'gajar ghas' / 'Congress grass' (folklore says it arrived in India via PL-480 wheat aid during 1955-56). Causes contact dermatitis, asthma, hay fever in humans; toxic to cattle. Now infests ~35 million hectares across India. Biological control attempted using the leaf-feeding beetle Zygogramma bicolorata (Mexico). Eichhornia = water hyacinth. Mikania = mile-a-minute weed. Prosopis = mesquite (vilayati kikar).

questions.stem: Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) is also nicknamed:

options.option_text: 'Bengal's Bane'
'Terror of Bengal'
'Mughal Weed'
'Devil's Daisy'

questions.explanation: Eichhornia crassipes — native to Amazon basin — introduced to India in the 1890s as an ornamental for ponds. Spread aggressively across Bengal waterways, choking fisheries and irrigation channels — hence 'Terror of Bengal'. It can double its biomass in two weeks under nutrient-rich conditions. Control methods — physical removal, herbicides (2,4-D), biological (Neochetina weevils). Some commercial uses — vermicompost, paper pulp, biogas — but elimination is far easier than utilisation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an invasive ALIEN fish species banned from culture in India under guidelines from ICAR / FSSAI?

options.option_text: Indian Major Carp (Catla)
African Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) and Thai Mangur
Rohu (Labeo rohita)
Common Carp (Cyprinus carpio)

questions.explanation: African / Thai Magur (Clarias gariepinus) — banned for culture in India since 2000 by NGT and reaffirmed by Supreme Court (2018). Reasons: (1) Outcompetes native magur (Clarias batrachus); (2) Carnivorous — eats native fish, frogs; (3) Grows fast in low-oxygen sewage water — biosecurity risk. Common Carp is naturalised; Catla, Rohu, Mrigal are native Indian Major Carps. Other banned exotics: Pacu (red-bellied piranha), Pirhana, Aligator gar.

questions.stem: 'Prosopis juliflora' — known in India as 'vilayati kikar' or 'angreji babool' — is an invasive species native to:

options.option_text: Australia
Mexico and Central America
South Africa
Madagascar

questions.explanation: Prosopis juliflora — drought-tolerant thorny tree from Mexico/Central America. Introduced to India in 1857 (Sind area, then Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu) for fuelwood and erosion control on degraded lands. It has now invaded grasslands and wetlands — depleting groundwater, replacing native flora. Punjabi name 'vilayati kikar' = 'foreign acacia'. In Tamil Nadu it covers >5 lakh ha. SC banned its felling without permits but TN and Rajasthan have programs to selectively remove it from biodiversity-sensitive areas.

questions.stem: Which Indian wildlife sanctuary is famously battling Mikania micrantha (mile-a-minute weed) that smothers native vegetation?

options.option_text: Gir, Gujarat
Kaziranga, Assam
Bandhavgarh, MP
Sariska, Rajasthan

questions.explanation: Mikania micrantha — fast-growing climbing vine from Central/South America — was introduced to NE India in the 1940s to camouflage Allied airfields during WWII. It now smothers grasslands and bushes in Kaziranga, Manas and surrounding NE forests, reducing fodder for rhinos, elephants and deer. Manual uprooting is the main control. Other Kaziranga IAS concerns — water hyacinth, alligator weed (Alternanthera philoxeroides). Climate-change-aided spread is documented.

questions.stem: The 'Invasive Species Specialist Group' (ISSG) — publisher of the globally cited '100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species' list — functions as a specialist group under which international body?

options.option_text: UN Environment Programme (UNEP), headquartered in Nairobi
International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity
World Wildlife Fund for Nature (WWF International)

questions.explanation: The ISSG operates under IUCN's Species Survival Commission (SSC) and hosts the Global Invasive Species Database (GISD). UNEP is the most common distractor as it coordinates major environmental conventions, but it does not host the ISSG. The CBD Secretariat is the treaty body that addresses IAS under Aichi Target 9 — a distinct institution from IUCN.

questions.stem: The Suckermouth Armoured Catfish (Pterygoplichthys spp.) — now breeding in the Yamuna, Cauvery, and Periyar rivers after escaping or being released from the aquarium trade — is originally native to:

options.option_text: Freshwater rivers and floodplains of central and South America
Slow-moving rivers and swamps of equatorial West Africa
Fast-flowing streams and rivers of Southeast Asian islands
Lake systems and wetland margins of eastern Australia

questions.explanation: Pterygoplichthys (family Loricariidae) is endemic to Amazonian and Orinoco river systems in South America — primarily Brazil and Argentina. Southeast Asia (C) is the most common wrong guess because many popular ornamental fish originate there, but Loricariid catfish are exclusively South American. It entered India through deliberate aquarium-trade release.

questions.stem: Salvinia molesta — the floating invasive fern notorious for doubling its biomass within two days and forming dense mats that deplete light and oxygen in Indian water bodies — is originally native to:

options.option_text: Tropical swamp forests of Central and West Africa
Subtropical river floodplains of south-eastern Brazil
Freshwater lake systems of southern India and Sri Lanka
Tidal wetlands and mangroves of the Philippine archipelago

questions.explanation: Salvinia molesta (giant salvinia) is native to south-eastern Brazil, specifically the Paraná River basin. Option C is a classic trap — India and Sri Lanka harbour several native salvinia species, leading candidates to assume S. molesta originated in South Asia. It is now a Category 1 noxious weed in Australia and has devastated wetlands across Kerala and Assam.

questions.stem: The Red-eared Slider (Trachemys scripta elegans) — a North American freshwater turtle now found breeding in Indian ponds and urban water bodies — spread to India almost exclusively through:

options.option_text: Deliberate release by fishery departments for aquatic weed control
Ballast water discharge from cargo ships at major Indian ports
Release of unwanted pets purchased from the reptile-aquarium trade
Intentional introduction for zoo breeding and genetic studies

questions.explanation: Red-eared sliders became globally invasive almost entirely through pet release: bought as hatchlings, they are discarded into local water bodies once they outgrow their tanks. IUCN lists the pet trade as the overwhelmingly dominant introduction pathway. Ballast water (B) is the standard pathway for marine and brackish invertebrate invaders, not freshwater reptiles sold in pet shops.

questions.stem: Invasive American Bullfrogs (Lithobates catesbeianus) are regarded as catastrophic for native amphibians worldwide partly because they act as asymptomatic reservoirs of:

options.option_text: Ranavirus, a DNA virus causing haemorrhagic skin lesions in frogs
Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis, the chytrid fungus causing chytridiomycosis
Saprolegnia parasitica, a water mould causing egg and gill disease
Ophidiomyces ophiodiicola, a skin-invading fungus targeting salamanders

questions.explanation: Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) causes chytridiomycosis, linked to the decline or extinction of over 200 amphibian species globally. American Bullfrogs tolerate Bd asymptomatically and spread it to susceptible native species. Ranavirus (A) is a genuine amphibian pathogen but is not the disease primarily associated with bullfrog-mediated spread. Option D, Ophidiomyces, is a snake fungal disease pathogen entirely unrelated to amphibians.

questions.stem: 'Invasional meltdown' — a term coined by Simberloff and Von Holle (1999) — describes the ecological scenario where:

options.option_text: Biocontrol agents accidentally eliminate native species alongside target invaders
Native species recover rapidly after a single keystone invasive is eradicated
Multiple alien species mutually facilitate each other's spread and establishment
An invader's niche contracts sharply due to native competitive resistance

questions.explanation: Invasional meltdown describes a positive feedback loop: each additional invasive species modifies habitat, suppresses native competitors, or provides food subsidies for other invaders, making further establishment progressively easier. Option B (rapid native recovery after eradication) describes 'biotic resistance', the conceptual opposite. Option A describes 'non-target effects' of biocontrol — a distinct conservation concern not related to inter-invader facilitation.

questions.stem: The 'Enemy Release Hypothesis' (ERH) in invasion biology proposes that introduced species gain a competitive edge in their new range primarily because:

options.option_text: Their high mutation rates generate locally adapted ecotypes within a few generations
They produce allelopathic root exudates that suppress native plant competitors
Climate warming opens novel thermal niches that alien species alone can exploit
They escape specialist predators, parasites, and pathogens left in their native range

questions.explanation: The ERH (Keane & Crawley, 2002) posits that invasive species thrive because the specialist natural enemies — herbivores, parasites, pathogens — that regulate their populations at home are absent in the introduced range. Option B describes allelopathy, a real mechanism observed in species like Garlic Mustard (Alliaria petiolata), but it is a separate hypothesis. Option A describes rapid local adaptation, a different and more recent invasion biology framework.
